item.title: Academy of Country Music CEO Damon Whiteside on the Awards Returning to Las Vegas and ‘Leaving on a High Note’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we're talking about the latest news in music. Today, we're focusing on the Academy of Country Music Awards, also known as the ACMs. I'm your host, and let's dive right in.
[Music transitions]
Host: The ACMs are keeping their supersized length for this year's show on May 17th. That's right, the ceremony will remain at 2 hours and 30 minutes, giving room for more performances and artists. According to ACM CEO Damon Whiteside, this decision was made because fans loved the extra time, and with a light commercial load, it's mostly wall-to-wall music.
[Short music break]
Host: Now, let's talk about the nominees. Megan Moroney is leading the pack with 9 nominations, followed closely by Miranda Lambert with 8. Ella Langley and Lainey Wilson are also up for 7 awards each. This year's nominees are dominated by newer acts, which is exciting to see. As Damon Whiteside says, the ACMs often recognize artists early in their careers, and it's cool to see a new crop of talent being recognized.
[Music transitions]
Host: The leading nominees also include Chris Stapleton with 6 nominations, and Zach Top, Cody Johnson, and Riley Green with 4 or 5 nominations each. Interestingly, there's no new duo or group category this year due to a lack of qualified candidates. But don't worry, it's expected to return next year.
[Short music break]
Host: Before we go, a few awards have already been announced. Jessie Jo Dillon is Songwriter of the Year, Tucker Wetmore is New Male Artist of the Year, Avery Anna is New Female Artist of the Year, and "Cuckoo" is Visual Media of the Year. The ACM Awards will be held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, and tickets are available now on AXS.com.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next episode.
